newsitem.title: USA: Clinton lead over Dole wider in Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton lead over Dole wider in Reuters poll.

text.p: President Bill Clinton widened his lead over Republican Bob Dole to above 12 points and is boosting Democratic chances in congressional races, the Reuter daily tracking poll said on Sunday.

The poll, conducted by John Zogby Group International, showed Clinton with 45.5 percent, Dole 32.9 percent and independent Ross Perot, 7 percent. Results were based on a three-day rolling average of surveys of more than 900 likely voters. The margin of error was 3.3 percentage points.

"If Clinton rises into double digits, he carries Congress in the 'generic' question," said pollster John Zogby, suggesting improved chances of Democrats regaining control of Congress riding on Clintobn's coattails.
Republicans captured control of both houses of Congress in 1994 for the first time in 40 years.
When respondents were asked which party's candidate they would support in their local congressional district, 38.6 percent said the Democrat and 33.8 percent said the Republican.
The lead between congressional parties has switched hands since daily surveys began Sept. 28. Usually, the margin between the two parties was less than two percentage points.
However, respondents were more evenly divided when asked which party should control the House of Representatives or Senate.
Clinton has widened his lead over Dole since Oct. 8 but showed the greatest growth in the past couple of days. Zogby said Perot nearly doubled his support in the same period.
